_what: Every public table with a client_id column that the authenticated role can reach and that carries no RESTRICTIVE policy asking the assignment scope (my_assigned_client_ids / can_access_client), with the reason. Held SHRINK-ONLY by tests/test_every_client_table_is_assignment_scoped_or_says_why_pg.py: a table that gains the scope must leave this file, and a new client table cannot join it as 'pending'. Kinds: parent = a policy of the table asks the named parent table, whose own policies carry the scope (verified); own = the named policy is the table's own rule (verified to exist); source = the assignment source itself; pending = firm policy only, with the ledger item that closes it. `children` is the second list, under the same rule: the tables with NO client_id of their own that hang from a client table and admit every member of the firm to every client's rows (a bare firm policy, no restrictive policy that reads the parent or asks the scope); an entry names the foreign-key parents and the ledger item that closes it, and leaves the file when the table follows its parent.

account_period_balances.why: its only policy asks client_id IN (SELECT id FROM clients), and clients carries the assignment scope, so a balance is as visible as its client

client_instructions.why: a Manager is firm-wide in the knowledge base and its instructions by design (docs/architecture/11-revenue-ops-and-knowledge.md); everyone below a Manager needs an assignment row

knowledge_articles.why: a Manager is firm-wide in the knowledge base by design (docs/architecture/11-revenue-ops-and-knowledge.md); a firm-level article has no client; everyone below a Manager needs an assignment row

notifications.why: a notification is its recipient's (user_id) and a Partner reads all; it is about a person, not about the client it names

reconciliation_findings.why: read by a Partner only and written by the server

reconciliation_runs.why: read by a Partner only and written by the server

user_client_assignments.why: it IS the assignment source: my_assigned_client_ids() and can_access_client read it as their owner, and migration 084 left it out of the scope on purpose; who may change it is migration 478's rule
